I need you guys to help me work through this conflict that I'm having about Mac Studios. 

I would love to wait and order the 512 GB variant of the M5 Ultra Studio and I think what they've built is pretty amazing.

So then the question becomes, is it really worth it to run a model with 40B active params? And if not, then why would you need more capacity? 

Is the 256GB not the sweet spot with a model like Qwen 3.8 Next? Only 6B active parameters is going to run far better on Apple silicon. 

I'm not convinced the trade off is worth it. Especially when you factor in concurrency. Thoughts?

with modern agentic tools and a much closer look, the picture looks totally different. the vast majority in models up to trillions of parameters are legible, and their circuits beautiful. many famous examples of tangled neurons turned out to be misunderstood. RT @Ready4Sushi: Etherbulb beta release for the ESP32-C3 E27 LED bulb and the SP530 RGB LED controller.

Your room is full of radio you never see: Wi-Fi, a phone talking to its earbuds, a smart plug on Zigbee, the cell tower down the road, an FPV drone in the park. Etherbulb turns a 15-dollar smart bulb into a lamp that shows you the air.

What it does
• Uses the ESP32-C3's Wi-Fi radio as a receive-only SDR (the ESP-SDR path found by ESPARGOS): 80 MS/s I/Q, 25 snapshots a second, 256-point FFT on the chip itself
• Hears 2.13–2.73 GHz: all Wi-Fi channels, Bluetooth, Zigbee/Thread, analog FPV video, LTE/5G Band 1, 7 and 38
• Classifies signals by shape* (early alpha)
• Blue for Bluetooth, green for Wi-Fi, any colour you pick for anything else. Stronger signal, brighter light
• Colour matrix in the dashboard: one row per signal, click a colour, set brightness and sensitivity, or drag a range on the live waterfall to make your own rule
• 26 presets from ExpressLRS to microwave ovens, plus 412 mobile-network blocks for 39 European countries, uplink and downlink
• Web dashboard served by the bulb: live waterfall, spectrum, log with router time, light and dark theme, works on a phone
• Wi-Fi and listening at the same time: the bulb stays on your network while it listens
• Idle light: a faint glow until its signal shows up
• Switch it off and on 3× for 30 min of Wi-Fi, 7× for a rescue network with the update page. After three crashes it boots the previous firmware by itself

LED strips too
The same firmware runs on the BTF SP530E strip controller (also ESP32-C3): five outputs, five strips, one per signal type, all on at once. One LED per MHz if you like.

Hardware
•12 W RGBCW E27 bulb, ESP32-C3 inside. Flashes over Wi-Fi, no screwdriver
• SP530E: first flash over UART,
